answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can join a marketplace, with the stake slashed if peers later prove duplicate identities. Think of reputation as a prism: one real history refracts into verifiable work, payments, and endorsements, while fake copies show only a thin delta between claimed activity and confirmed results. A bridge of independent attestations then connects that history across services, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes and a thousand consistent records, while an honest newcomer pays only once.
